definition_zh: 等级；地位；军衔；行列；把…分等级；位居
definition_en: a position on a scale of importance or quality; an official grade, especially in the armed forces; a row of people or things; to place people or things in order; to hold a particular position
core_image: 一排士兵按高矮站成的笔直队列
scene: 操场上，士兵们按个头从高到矮站成一条直线，队伍整齐得像尺子画出来。The captain held the rank of major for many years.
sceneCN: 这里 rank 是「军衔」（第 2 个义项：军队中的正式等级）；句意为这位上尉多年保持少校军衔。画面里可留意：整齐的队伍、按身高排成的直线、军装的肩章。

derivatives.zh: rank 加 -ing，指名次、排名
rank 加 -ed，指被排定名次的
out- 与 rank 复合，指地位高于
high 与 ranking 复合，指级别高的

senses.title: A position on a scale
senses.definition: a position on a scale of importance, quality or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性、质量或成就的尺度上所居的位置
senses.example: She reached the top rank of her profession.
senses.exampleCN: 她达到了本行业的最高等级。
senses.why: A row of soldiers fixes each person in a place, and that fixed place became a measure of standing.
senses.whyCN: 一排士兵把每个人固定在某个位置，这个固定位置便成了地位的衡量。

senses.title: An official grade
senses.definition: an official grade held by a member of the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装部队成员所持的正式等级
senses.example: The captain held the rank of major.
senses.exampleCN: 这位上尉持有少校军衔。
senses.why: Armies number their rows from bottom to top, so the place a soldier occupies became his official grade.
senses.whyCN: 军队把队列自下而上编号，因此士兵所占的位置便成了他的正式等级。

senses.title: A row of people or things
senses.definition: a row of people or things placed side by side
senses.definitionCN: 并排而立的一排人或物
senses.example: The chairs stood in a neat rank along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子沿墙排成整齐的一行。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a row, the line in which people or objects are drawn up.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是一排，即人或物被排成的直线。

senses.title: To place in order
senses.definition: to arrange people or things in order according to quality or importance
senses.definitionCN: 按质量或重要性把人或物排成次序
senses.example: The judges ranked the entries from best to worst.
senses.exampleCN: 评委把参赛作品从优到劣排出名次。
senses.why: If a rank is a row, to rank is to put things into that row in their proper places.
senses.whyCN: 既然 rank 是一行，to rank 就是把事物各归其位地排进那一行。

senses.title: To hold a position
senses.definition: to have a particular position in a scale, list or group
senses.definitionCN: 在尺度、名单或群体中占据特定位置
senses.example: The university ranks among the best in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学位居全国最好的大学之列。
senses.why: From the act of placing came the state of being placed, so a thing can rank, that is, stand somewhere in the order.
senses.whyCN: 从「摆放」的动作生出「被摆放」的状态，因此某物可以 rank，即在次序中站于某处。

intro.en: Rank comes from Old French ranc, a row, probably from the same Frankish source as range; a row of soldiers became a scale of official grades.
intro.cn: rank 来自古法语 ranc（一行），可能与 range 同出法兰克语；一排士兵后来变成了等级阶梯。

items.en: Old French ranc meant a row or line, especially a row of soldiers.
items.cn: 古法语 ranc 意为一行或一列，尤指一排士兵。

items.en: The word is traced to a Frankish term for a circle or band of men, the same source as range.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到法兰克语中表示一圈或一队人的词，与 range 同源。

items.en: Middle English rank kept both the row and the military line, and added the idea of a grade.
items.cn: 中古英语 rank 既保留「一排」与军阵的线，又加上了等级的意思。

items.en: Because a formation places each soldier in a fixed spot, rank came to mean a soldier's official grade.
items.cn: 由于队列把每个士兵放在固定位置，rank 便引申为士兵的正式等级。

items.en: Modern English ranks people and things by quality, and uses the verb to rank for placing and for holding a place.
items.cn: 现代英语按质量给人或物排等级，并用动词 rank 表示排位和位居。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers row words and close forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for grade and standing.
note.cn: 形近组收表示行列的词与近形词；近义组收表示等级与地位的词。

entries.definition: A row or extent, the close cousin of rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一行或范围，rank 的近亲。

entries.definition: A position on a list of results.
A person who patrols a wild area.
A level of quality or rank.
A person's social or official standing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的社会地位或官方身份。

entries.definition: A place in a scale or order.
entries.definitionCN: 在尺度或次序中的位置。

entries.definition: A division based on quality or rank.
entries.definitionCN: 按质量或等级划分的类别。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a row of bodies, then becomes the place each body occupies, and finally the act and state of standing somewhere in an order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一排身体开始，变成每具身体所占的位置，最后成为「处于某个次序位置」的动作与状态。

normal.en: Rank and range come from the same old word for a row.
normal.cn: rank 与 range 同出表示「一行」的那个古词。

normal.en: A rank of soldiers is a row; an officer's rank is his place in that row.
normal.cn: 士兵的 rank 是一排；军官的 rank 是他在这一排里的位置。

normal.en: To rank first is to stand at the head of the row.
normal.cn: to rank first 就是站在这支队伍的最前头。

normal.en: Rank and file names the ordinary soldiers who stand in the rows.
normal.cn: rank and file 指站在队列里的普通士兵。

normal.en: To rank something is to put it into its proper place in the line.
normal.cn: 给某物 rank 就是把它放到队列中合适的位置。

abstract.en: Rank measures where you stand, not who you are.
abstract.cn: rank 衡量的是你站在哪里，而不是你是谁。

abstract.en: A list ranks names the way a formation ranks bodies, by a fixed order.
abstract.cn: 名单给名字排名，正如队列给身体排名，都依一种固定次序。

abstract.en: To outrank someone is to stand one step nearer the front.
abstract.cn: outrank 某人，就是比他站得离排头更近一步。

examples.en: He rose to the rank of colonel.
examples.cn: 他升到了上校军衔。

examples.en: The university ranks among the best in the country.
examples.cn: 这所大学位居全国最好的大学之列。

examples.en: The students were ranked by their test scores.
examples.cn: 学生们按考试成绩被排了名次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「队伍排成一排」——rank 本是一行士兵，后来引申为等级与军衔。

root: 古法语 ranc（一行）→ 中古英语 rank → 现代英语 rank；与 range 同源，可能出自法兰克语「一圈人」。同族有 ranking、ranked、outrank。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a row of bodies; the senses move from a grade of standing to a military grade, to the row itself, and then to the act and state of ordering.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一排身体；义项从地位等级，到军衔，再到行列本身，最后到排序的动作与状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soldiers standing shoulder to shoulder in a straight line, each at a fixed spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：士兵肩并肩站成一条直线，每人各占一个固定位置。

chain: A FIXED SPOT IN THE ROW

branches.en: soldiers standing shoulder to shoulder
steps of a ladder from low to high
stripes on a uniform sleeve
cards sorted by number
a name near the top of a list
branches.cn: 名单接近顶端的一个名字

intro.en: The word is a borrowing from Old French, and its family is built with English suffixes, a prefix and fixed phrases.
intro.cn: 这个词借自古法语，其词族由英语后缀、一个前缀与固定短语构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word; the older root is Frankish.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录；更早的词根是法兰克语。

definition_zh: 迅速的；急剧的；急流
definition_en: moving or happening very quickly; happening suddenly and to a great degree; a part of a river where the water flows fast and rough over rocks
core_image: 河水在乱石间奔涌成一道白色的急流
scene: 山谷里的河水撞上乱石，翻起白色的浪头，一路奔涌而下。The river's rapid current swept the boat downstream in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 rapid 是「迅速的」（第 1 个义项：移动或发生得极快）；句意为河中湍急的水流几秒钟就把小船冲向下游。画面里可留意：翻白的浪头、乱石、被冲走的小船。

derivatives.zh: rapid 加 -ly，指迅速地
rapid 加 -ity，指迅速、快捷
rapid 加 -s，指河中湍急的一段
rapid 加 -ness，指迅速的状态

senses.title: Moving very quickly
senses.definition: moving or happening at great speed
senses.definitionCN: 以极快的速度移动或发生
senses.example: The country has seen rapid economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家经历了迅速的经济增长。
senses.why: Latin rapidus described anything carried along swiftly, and the word kept that plain sense of speed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rapidus 形容任何被迅速带走之物，这个词保留了这层朴素的「快」。

senses.title: Sudden and great in degree
senses.definition: happening suddenly and to a large degree, used especially of change
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生且幅度很大，尤用于变化
senses.example: A rapid change in the weather caught the climbers off guard.
senses.exampleCN: 天气的急剧变化让登山者措手不及。
senses.why: Something carried away fast can also change fast, so rapid extended from speed of motion to speed of change.
senses.whyCN: 被迅速带走之物也会迅速改变，于是 rapid 从运动之快扩展到变化之快。

senses.title: Fast rough water
senses.definition: a stretch of river where the water runs fast and breaks over rocks
senses.definitionCN: 河水中流得很快、在岩石上翻涌的一段
senses.example: The raft bounced through the rapids.
senses.exampleCN: 木筏在急流中颠簸而过。
senses.why: The same image of water seized and carried along named the place in a river where the current runs hardest.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「水被卷走」的意象，命名了河中水流最猛的那一段。

intro.en: Rapid goes back to Latin rapere, to seize and carry away; what is rapid is literally carried along at speed.
intro.cn: rapid 可追溯到拉丁语 rapere（抓住并带走）；被 rapid 形容之物，字面上就是被迅速卷走的。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off, and it pictured force dragging something away.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住并带走，画面是力量把某物拖走。

items.en: Rapidus described anything carried along swiftly, from a rushing river to a fast flight.
items.cn: rapidus 形容任何被迅速带走之物，从奔腾的河到飞快的飞行。

items.en: Old French took the Latin word as rapide and kept the sense of great speed.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词借作 rapide，保留了「极快」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rapid applied the word to motion, to events, and to rivers that run fast.
items.cn: 中古英语 rapid 把这个词用于运动、事件，以及流得快的河。

items.en: Modern English uses rapid for quick motion and quick change, and the plural rapids for rough, fast water.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rapid 指快速运动与快速变化，用复数 rapids 指湍急的水流。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and one word from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers ordinary words for speed.
note.cn: 形近组收同根的形式与一个同源词；近义组收表示速度的常用词。

entries.definition: A stretch of fast, rough river water.
The act of seizing property by force, from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力夺取财物，同一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: Moving or happening at high speed.
Moving or done in a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 在短时间内移动或完成的。
移动极快，常含顺畅之意。

normalIntro.en: The word pictures things seized and carried along; from that force come the senses of fast motion, fast change and fast water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的画面是被抓住并卷走的东西；从这股力量生出快速运动、快速变化与湍急水流三层意思。

normal.en: Rapid and rapere share the image of something seized and carried off at speed.
normal.cn: rapid 与 rapere 共享「某物被抓住并迅速卷走」的画面。

normal.en: Rapids are the parts of a river where the water itself runs fast.
normal.cn: rapids 就是河中水本身流得最快的地方。

normal.en: Rapid growth and rapid change both describe movement in time, not in space.
normal.cn: rapid growth 与 rapid change 描述的都是时间中的移动，而不是空间中的移动。

normal.en: Rapid is stronger than quick: it suggests real force behind the speed.
normal.cn: rapid 比 quick 更强，暗含速度背后有一股真实的力量。

normal.en: The same root gives rapine, the taking of goods by force.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 rapine，即用武力夺取财物。

abstract.en: Speed that carries things away is the oldest sense of rapid.
abstract.cn: 「把东西卷走的快」是 rapid 最古老的意思。

abstract.en: We call change rapid when it moves faster than we can follow.
abstract.cn: 当变化快过我们跟上的速度，我们才称它 rapid。

abstract.en: A rapid is water in a hurry, and that is the word's whole picture.
abstract.cn: 急流是匆匆赶路的水，这就是这个词的全部画面。

examples.en: The country has seen rapid economic growth.
examples.cn: 这个国家经历了迅速的经济增长。

examples.en: A rapid change in the weather caught the climbers off guard.
examples.cn: 天气的急剧变化让登山者措手不及。

examples.en: The raft bounced through the rapids.
examples.cn: 木筏在急流中颠簸而过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拉皮的」——被人拽着飞快拖走，记住 rapid 是迅速的。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（抓住带走）→ rapidus（被迅速带走的）→ 古法语 rapide → 现代英语 rapid；同族有 rapidly、rapidity、rapids。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being seized and carried along; the senses divide into fast motion, fast change, and fast rough water.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被抓住并卷走」；义项分为快速运动、快速变化与湍急的水流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current of white water tearing through rocks and dragging everything with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股白色的水流撕开乱石，把一切都拖走。

branches.en: a sprinter leaving the blocks
a price line climbing steeply
white water breaking over rocks
speed in motion and speed in change
a fast runner and a fast river
branches.cn: 飞快的奔跑者与湍急的河流

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes and compounds on the same root.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由同一词根上的英语后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the word its root: rapere, to seize, and rapidus, carried swiftly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给了这个词词根：rapere（抓住）与 rapidus（被迅速带走）。

definition_zh: 迅速地；急剧地；接连不断地
definition_en: at great speed; within a short time and to a great degree; one after another in quick succession
core_image: 秒针绕着表盘飞速转圈
scene: 仪表盘上的指针一格接一格地跳动，数字不断向上翻。Prices rose rapidly during the shortage.
sceneCN: 这里 rapidly 是「迅速地」（第 1 个义项：以极快的速度）；句意为短缺期间物价迅速上涨。画面里可留意：跳动的指针、不断上翻的数字。

pos.zh: 迅速地；急剧地；接连不断地

derivatives.zh: rapidly 去掉 -ly，指迅速的
rapid 加 -ity，指迅速、快捷
rapid 加 -s，指河中湍急的一段

senses.title: At great speed
senses.definition: at great speed, of movement or action
senses.definitionCN: 移动或行动以极快的速度
senses.example: Prices rose rapidly during the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 短缺期间物价迅速上涨。
senses.why: Rapidly is rapid plus the adverb ending, so it describes an action done with the speed that rapid names.
senses.whyCN: rapidly 是 rapid 加副词词尾，因此它描述以 rapid 所指的那种速度完成的动作。

senses.title: Sharply in a short time
senses.definition: suddenly and to a great degree within a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内突然而大幅度地
senses.example: The situation changed rapidly after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告发布后局势急剧变化。
senses.why: Because rapid also means sudden in degree, the adverb can describe change that is sharp as well as fast.
senses.whyCN: 由于 rapid 也指幅度上的突然，这个副词既能描述快，也能描述变得剧烈。

senses.title: One after another
senses.definition: in quick succession, with little pause between events
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个，事件之间几乎没有停顿
senses.example: Reports came rapidly, one after another.
senses.exampleCN: 报告接连不断地传来。
senses.why: When things follow at great speed, the adverb marks not one fast act but a stream of them in quick succession.
senses.whyCN: 当事物以极快速度接连而来，这个副词标记的不是一个快动作，而是一连串紧接的动作。

intro.en: Rapidly is rapid with the English adverb ending -ly, and rapid itself goes back to Latin rapere, to seize and carry away.
intro.cn: rapidly 是 rapid 加上英语副词词尾 -ly，而 rapid 本身可追溯到拉丁语 rapere（抓住并带走）。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off, the picture behind all forms of this family.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住并带走，是整个词族背后的画面。

items.en: Rapidus described what is carried along swiftly, and English borrowed it as rapid.
items.cn: rapidus 形容被迅速带走之物，英语把它借作 rapid。

items.en: English kept rapid as an adjective of speed before any adverb was formed from it.
items.cn: 英语先把 rapid 作为表示速度的形容词保留下来，之后才由它构成副词。

items.en: The old English ending -lice became -ly, which turns an adjective into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -lice 演变为 -ly，把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English uses rapidly for speed, for sharp change, and for events that follow in quick succession.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rapidly 表示速度、急剧变化，以及紧接而来的事件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base word and its close forms; the near-meaning group gathers common adverbs of speed.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的原形与近形；近义组收常用的速度副词。

entries.definition: Fast, rough water in a river.

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds manner to the adjective rapid, so it tells how fast an action is done, how sharp a change is, or how closely events follow.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词给形容词 rapid 加上「方式」，说明动作做得多快、变化多剧烈，或事件跟得多紧。

normal.en: Rapidly is simply rapid with the adverb ending -ly.
normal.cn: rapidly 就是 rapid 加上副词词尾 -ly。

normal.en: Rapidly and quickly both mean at speed, but rapidly sounds more formal and more forceful.
normal.cn: rapidly 与 quickly 都表示快速，但 rapidly 更正式、更有力。

normal.en: Prices that rise rapidly climb a long way in a short time.
normal.cn: rise rapidly 的物价在短时间内涨了很多。

normal.en: Events that follow rapidly come one after another without pause.
normal.cn: follow rapidly 的事件一个接一个，没有停顿。

normal.en: The root rapere, to seize, is still visible in the force of rapidly.
normal.cn: 词根 rapere（抓住）在 rapidly 的力量感里仍然看得见。

abstract.en: Rapidly measures not distance but the rate at which time is filled.
abstract.cn: rapidly 衡量的不是距离，而是时间被填满的速率。

abstract.en: What happens rapidly often outruns our ability to react.
abstract.cn: 发生得 rapidly 的事，常常快过我们反应的能力。

abstract.en: To change rapidly is to move faster than the old shape can hold.
abstract.cn: 变化 rapidly，就是动得比旧形态所能容纳的更快。

examples.en: The situation changed rapidly after the announcement.
examples.cn: 公告发布后局势迅速变化。

examples.en: The disease spread rapidly through the crowded camp.
examples.cn: 疾病在拥挤的营地中迅速传播。

examples.en: Reports came rapidly, one after another.
examples.cn: 报告接连不断地传来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「表针飞转」——指针一圈圈飞快地转，记住 rapidly 是迅速地。

root: 拉丁语 rapere → rapidus → 英语 rapid + 副词后缀 -ly → rapidly；同族有 rapid、rapidity、rapids。

sensesIntro.en: The core is speed in action; the senses divide into plain speed, sharp change in a short time, and events following one another closely.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是动作中的速度；义项分为单纯的速度、短时间内的急剧变化，以及紧接而来的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock hand spinning round the dial, faster than the eye can follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟表指针绕表盘飞转，快得眼睛跟不上。

branches.en: a clock hand spinning fast
a steeply rising graph
a row of lights flashing in turn
speed and suddenness together
branches.cn: 速度与突然性合在一起

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with two English layers, the adjective rapid and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加两层英语成分：形容词 rapid 与副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the root: rapere, to seize, and rapidus, carried swiftly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给出词根：rapere（抓住）与 rapidus（被迅速带走）。

definition_zh: 稀有的；罕见的；半熟的；稀薄的
definition_en: not common or not happening often; cooked lightly so the inside stays red; thin and not dense, of air
core_image: 空荡展厅里唯一一件孤零零的展品
scene: 空旷的展厅里只摆着一件展品，四周安静得能听见脚步。Such a rare bird is seen only once in a lifetime.
sceneCN: 这里 rare 是「稀有的」（第 1 个义项：不常见、很少发生）；句意为这样稀有的鸟一生只能见到一次。画面里可留意：空荡的展厅、唯一的展品、安静的脚步。

pos.zh: 稀有的；罕见的；半熟的；稀薄的

derivatives.zh: rare 加 -ly，指很少、不常
rare 加 -ity，指罕见、珍品
rare 加 -fy 与 -ed，指变得稀薄的
rare 加 -er，指更罕见的

senses.title: Uncommon
senses.definition: not found, seen or happening often; existing in small numbers
senses.definitionCN: 不常被发现、看见或发生；数量很少
senses.example: Such a rare bird is seen only once in a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 这样稀有的鸟一生只能见到一次。
senses.why: Latin rarus meant thinly spread, and the English word kept that picture of something scattered rather than plentiful.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rarus 意为分布稀疏，英语这个词保留了「零落而非充裕」的画面。

senses.title: Lightly cooked
senses.definition: cooked for a short time so that the inside is still red
senses.definitionCN: 烹制时间很短，内部仍然透红
senses.example: He likes his steak rare.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢半熟的牛排。
senses.why: English cooks used rare for meat left briefly on the heat, and the sense has stayed fixed in the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的厨师用 rare 指在火上停留很短的肉，这层意思一直固定在厨房里。

senses.title: Thin, of air
senses.definition: thin and not dense, used especially of air at high places
senses.definitionCN: 稀薄而不浓密，尤用于高处的空气
senses.example: The air grows rare as you climb higher.
senses.exampleCN: 越往上爬，空气越稀薄。
senses.why: Air that is thinly spread is close to the original sense of rarus, so the word could describe atmosphere as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 分布稀疏的空气贴近 rarus 的本义，因此这个词既能形容物件，也能形容大气。

intro.en: Rare comes from Latin rarus, thinly spread or uncommon, and English added the senses of thin air and lightly cooked meat.
intro.cn: rare 来自拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏或不常见），英语又添上稀薄空气与半熟肉这两层意思。

items.en: Rarus meant thinly spread or uncommon, and it described both sparse things and rare events.
items.cn: rarus 意为分布稀疏或不常见，既形容稀疏之物，也形容罕见之事。

items.en: Old French borrowed it as rare and kept the sense of something seldom found.
items.cn: 古法语把它借作 rare，保留「难得一见」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rare applied the word to uncommon things and to thin air.
items.cn: 中古英语 rare 把这个词用于罕见之物与稀薄的空气。

items.en: The sense of lightly cooked meat grew in English kitchens, where rare described meat left briefly on the heat.
items.cn: 半熟肉的意思在英语的厨房里长成，rare 指在火上停留很短的肉。

items.en: Modern English uses rare for uncommon things, thin air, and meat cooked only briefly.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rare 指罕见之物、稀薄的空气，以及只略加烹制的肉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base form and its close relatives; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is hard to find.
note.cn: 形近组收本词原形与近亲；近义组收表示「难觅」的词。

entries.definition: Something uncommon, or the state of being uncommon.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见之物，或罕见的状态。

entries.definition: Hard to find because there is little of it.
Not usual or not often seen.
Not ordinary, often in a noticeable way.
entries.definitionCN: 不普通的，常带引人注目之意。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with scarcity, then takes in thin air and meat left briefly on the fire.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「稀少」开始，随后纳入稀薄的空气与在火上略过的肉。

normal.en: Rare and rarus both begin with the idea of something thinly spread.
normal.cn: rare 与 rarus 都从「某物分布稀疏」这一想法开始。

normal.en: A rare bird is one you seldom see, not one that cannot exist.
normal.cn: rare bird 是你很少见到的鸟，而不是不可能存在的鸟。

normal.en: Rare steak is cooked briefly, so the centre stays red.
normal.cn: rare steak 煎得很快，所以中心仍是红的。

normal.en: Rare air is thin air, as on a high mountain.
normal.cn: rare air 是稀薄的空气，就像高山上那样。

normal.en: Rarity is the noun and rarely the adverb, and both keep the sense of not often.
normal.cn: rarity 是名词，rarely 是副词，两者都保留「不常」的意思。

abstract.en: Rare things matter because they are few, not because they are better.
abstract.cn: 稀有之物重要，是因为它们少，而不是因为它们更好。

abstract.en: What is rare is defined by the many common things around it.
abstract.cn: 稀有之物是由周围众多常见之物界定出来的。

abstract.en: To call a moment rare is to say it will not come again soon.
abstract.cn: 称一个时刻 rare，是说它不会很快再来。

examples.en: This is a rare species found only on one island.
examples.cn: 这是只在一座岛上才能找到的稀有物种。

examples.en: He likes his steak rare.
examples.cn: 他喜欢半熟的牛排。

examples.en: The air grows rare as you climb higher.
examples.cn: 越往上爬，空气越稀薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「孤品」——展厅里只此一件，rare 就是稀有的、罕见的。

root: 拉丁语 rarus（稀疏、罕见）→ 古法语 rare → 现代英语 rare；同族有 rarely、rarity、rarefied。

sensesIntro.en: The core is scarcity; the senses divide into uncommon things, meat cooked briefly, and thin air.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「稀少」；义项分为罕见之物、略加烹制的肉，以及稀薄的空气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lonely object in a great empty hall.
core.cn: 核心意象：空荡大厅里孤零零的一件物品。

branches.en: a single gem in an empty hall
branches.cn: 空展厅里孤零零的一颗宝石

branches.en: a steak red at the centre
mountain air that is hard to breathe
branches.cn: 让人呼吸吃力的山地稀薄空气

branches.en: scarcity of things and scarcity of air
branches.cn: 物的稀少与空气的稀薄

branches.en: uncommon in supply and uncommon in cooking
branches.cn: 数量上的罕见与烹制上的半熟

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes on the same root.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由同一词根上的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin rarus, thinly spread, is the recorded source of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏）是这个词有记录可考的词源。

items.meaning: an uncommon kind of animal or plant

definition_zh: 很少；不常；难得；罕见地
definition_en: not often; hardly ever; in an uncommon manner
core_image: 日历上大片空白的格子，只偶尔落下一笔
scene: 日历翻过一页又一页，大多数格子都是空白的。She rarely speaks in front of a crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 rarely 是「很少」（第 1 个义项：不常发生）；句意为她很少在众人面前讲话。画面里可留意：大片空白的日历格、偶尔的一点墨迹。

derivatives.zh: rarely 去掉 -ly，指稀有的、罕见的
rare 加 -ity，指罕见、珍品
rare 加 -fy 与 -ed，指变得稀薄的

senses.title: Not often
senses.definition: not often, of an action or event
senses.definitionCN: 动作或事件不常发生
senses.example: She rarely speaks in front of a crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她很少在众人面前讲话。
senses.why: Rarely is rare with the adverb ending, so it says that something happens in a scarce, uncommon way.
senses.whyCN: rarely 是 rare 加副词词尾，说明某事以稀少、不常见的方式发生。

senses.title: Hardly ever
senses.definition: almost never, a stronger degree of the same idea
senses.definitionCN: 几乎从不，是同一意思的更强程度
senses.example: Such storms rarely reach this coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的风暴难得抵达这片海岸。
senses.why: When the adverb is stressed or paired with if ever, it moves from seldom to almost never.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词被重读或与 if ever 连用时，它就从「很少」推向「几乎从不」。

senses.title: In an uncommon way
senses.definition: in a manner that is uncommon, used in formal or literary style
senses.definitionCN: 以一种不常见的方式，用于正式或书面语体
senses.example: The word is rarely used in speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在口语中罕见地使用。
senses.why: The bare sense of rare is uncommon, and the adverb can still point at the manner itself rather than at frequency.
senses.whyCN: rare 的本义就是不常见，副词仍可指向方式本身，而不只是频率。

intro.en: Rarely is rare with the English adverb ending -ly, and rare goes back to Latin rarus, thinly spread.
intro.cn: rarely 是 rare 加上英语副词词尾 -ly，而 rare 可追溯到拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏）。

items.en: Rarus meant thinly spread or uncommon, the root shared with rare.
items.cn: rarus 意为分布稀疏或不常见，是与 rare 共有的词根。

items.en: English formed the adjective rare from the Latin word, meaning seldom found.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词构成形容词 rare，意为难得一见。

items.en: The ending -ly turned rare into an adverb meaning in a rare manner, hence not often.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把 rare 变成副词，意为以稀少的方式，因此就是「不常」。

items.en: Middle English used rarely for what happens seldom, and the word settled into everyday speech.
items.cn: 中古英语用 rarely 指很少发生的事，这个词逐渐进入日常语言。

items.en: Modern English uses rarely as the plain adverb of not often, and in formal style for in an uncommon way.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rarely 作「不常」的普通副词，并在正式文体中表示「以不常见的方式」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base word and its relatives; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of low frequency.
note.cn: 形近组收本词原形与近亲；近义组收表示低频的副词。

normalIntro.en: The adverb works on the adjective rare and turns scarcity into frequency: what is done in a rare way is done seldom.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词把形容词 rare 的稀少变成频率：以稀少方式做的事，就是很少做。

normal.en: Rarely is rare with -ly: what happens in a rare way happens seldom.
normal.cn: rarely 是 rare 加 -ly：以稀少方式发生的事就是很少发生。

normal.en: Rarely and seldom mean the same, but rarely is the more common adverb in writing.
normal.cn: rarely 与 seldom 同义，但 rarely 在书面语中更常用。

normal.en: Rarely is stronger when it means hardly ever, close to never.
normal.cn: 当 rarely 意为 hardly ever 时更强，接近 never。

normal.en: She rarely speaks means the speaking is the exception, not the rule.
normal.cn: She rarely speaks 意为开口是例外，不是常态。

normal.en: The word keeps the Latin picture of something thinly spread across time.
normal.cn: 这个词保留了拉丁语「某物在时间中分布稀疏」的画面。

abstract.en: Rarely marks the gaps in a pattern, not the pattern itself.
abstract.cn: rarely 标记的是图案中的空隙，而不是图案本身。

abstract.en: What happens rarely is noticed precisely because it is not routine.
abstract.cn: 很少发生的事之所以被注意到，正因为它不是常规。

abstract.en: To say rarely is to measure absence more than presence.
abstract.cn: 说 rarely，衡量的缺席多于在场。

examples.en: She rarely speaks in front of a crowd.
examples.cn: 她很少在众人面前讲话。

examples.en: Such storms rarely reach this coast.
examples.cn: 这样的风暴难得抵达这片海岸。

examples.en: He rarely, if ever, loses his temper.
examples.cn: 他几乎从不发脾气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「空白的日历」——一格又一格都没写字，rarely 就是很少、不常。

root: 拉丁语 rarus（稀疏、罕见）→ 英语 rare + 副词后缀 -ly → rarely；同族有 rare、rarity、rarefied。

sensesIntro.en: The core is low frequency; the senses divide into plain not-often, almost-never, and the formal sense of doing something in an uncommon way.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是低频；义项分为普通的「不常」、更强的「几乎从不」，以及正式的「以不常见方式」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: calendar squares left blank, with only an occasional mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上大片的空白格子，只偶尔有一笔。

branches.en: blank squares on a calendar
branches.cn: 日历上大片空白的格子

branches.en: a door that almost never opens
a word used only in formal writing
branches.cn: 只在正式文字中使用的词

branches.en: seldom and almost never
an act almost never done, done in an odd way
branches.cn: 几乎不做的事，以古怪方式做

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with two English layers, the adjective rare and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加两层英语成分：形容词 rare 与副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin rarus, thinly spread, is the recorded source of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 比率；速率；价格；费率；评价；认为
definition_en: a measure of how often or how fast something happens; a fixed charge or price; to judge the value or quality of something; to consider someone or something in a particular way
core_image: 仪表盘上按固定间隔跳动的指针
scene: 实验室的仪器每隔一会儿跳动一次，屏幕上留下一串均匀的数字。The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 rate 是「速率」（第 1 个义项：某事物发生的频繁程度或快慢）；句意为跑步者爬坡时心率上升。画面里可留意：规律跳动的仪器、屏幕上均匀的数字。

derivatives.zh: rate 加 -ing，指评分、评级
rate 加 -ed，指被评为某种等级的
与 rate 同源的拉丁词，指两个数量之比
over- 与 rate 复合，指高估

senses.title: A measure of frequency or speed
senses.definition: a measure of how often or how fast something happens, often per unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 衡量某事发生频率或快慢的量，常以单位时间为准
senses.example: The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步者爬坡时心率上升。
senses.why: Rate began as a settled, calculated amount, and measuring how often something happens is exactly such a calculation.
senses.whyCN: rate 最初指算定的数量，而衡量某事发生多频繁，正属这类计算。

senses.title: A fixed price or charge
senses.definition: a fixed amount charged for a service, a room or a unit of goods
senses.definitionCN: 为服务、房间或单位商品收取的固定金额
senses.example: The hotel charges a nightly rate of two hundred pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店每晚收费两百英镑。
senses.why: A rate is a sum fixed by agreement or rule, so the word naturally named the price set for a service.
senses.whyCN: rate 是按约定或规则定下的数额，这个词便自然用来指为服务定出的价格。

senses.title: To judge value
senses.definition: to judge the value, quality or performance of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 评判某人或某物的价值、质量或表现
senses.example: Critics rated the film highly.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人给这部影片很高评价。
senses.why: Once a rate was a fixed measure, the verb could mean to place something at a particular point on that measure.
senses.whyCN: rate 既是一种固定的衡量，动词便可指把某物放到这一尺度上的特定位置。

senses.title: To consider as
senses.definition: to regard someone or something as having a particular quality or standing
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物看作具有某种品质或地位
senses.example: He is rated as one of the best players.
senses.exampleCN: 他被认为是最好的球员之一。
senses.why: Judging a thing easily becomes placing it in a class, so to rate came to mean to regard something as being of a certain kind.
senses.whyCN: 评判一物很容易变成把它归入某一类，于是 to rate 逐渐意为「把某物看作某类」。

intro.en: Rate comes from Latin rata, fixed or settled by reckoning, from reri, to reckon; Old French passed it to English as a fixed share or charge.
intro.cn: rate 来自拉丁语 rata（经计算而确定的），源自动词 reri（计算、思考）；古法语把它作为固定的份额或费用传给英语。

items.en: Rata meant fixed or settled, of a sum that had been worked out and agreed.
items.cn: rata 意为确定、算定，指经过计算并获同意的一笔数额。

items.en: The root reri meant to reckon or think, so rata was what had been calculated.
items.cn: 词根 reri 意为计算或思考，因此 rata 就是被算出来的东西。

items.en: Old French rate carried the idea of a fixed share or a charge to be paid.
items.cn: 古法语 rate 带着「固定份额」或「应缴费用」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rate used the word for a fixed charge and for a measured proportion.
items.cn: 中古英语 rate 既指固定费用，也指被计量出的比例。

items.en: Modern English keeps rate for a measured proportion and a price, and adds the verb to rate, meaning to judge.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 rate 表示测得的比例与价格，并加上动词 rate，意为评判。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived forms and one confusing neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers words for speed, proportion and charge.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与一个易混词；近义组收表示速度、比例与收费的词。

entries.definition: Judged to have a certain quality.
A small rodent, a different word.
The rate at which something moves.
The speed at which something happens.
A part in relation to the whole.
The price asked for a service.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a reckoned, fixed amount, then splits into a measured proportion, a set price and the act of judging.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「算定的数额」开始，随后分成测得的比例、定好的价格与评判的行为。

normal.en: Rate and ratio share a Latin root meaning to reckon.
normal.cn: rate 与 ratio 共有表示「计算」的拉丁词根。

normal.en: A heart rate counts beats per minute, a rate per unit of time.
normal.cn: heart rate 数的是每分钟的跳动，即每单位时间的速率。

normal.en: A hotel rate is a fixed price for a room.
normal.cn: hotel rate 是一间房的固定价格。

normal.en: To rate a film is to give it a score.
normal.cn: to rate a film 就是给它打分。

normal.en: Rat and rate look alike but a rat is an animal and a rate is a measure.
normal.cn: rat 与 rate 形近，但 rat 是动物，rate 是度量。

abstract.en: A rate turns the flow of time into a number you can compare.
abstract.cn: rate 把时间的流动变成一个可以比较的数字。

abstract.en: To rate something is to turn a judgment into a place on a scale.
abstract.cn: 给某物 rate，就是把一次判断变成尺度上的一个位置。

abstract.en: Every rate hides a choice of what to count and over how long.
abstract.cn: 每一个 rate 背后都藏着「数什么、数多久」的选择。

examples.en: The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
examples.cn: 跑步者爬坡时心率上升。

examples.en: The hotel charges a nightly rate of two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 这家酒店每晚收费两百英镑。

examples.en: Critics rated the film highly.
examples.cn: 影评人给这部影片很高评价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞特」——仪表上均匀跳动的数字，记住 rate 是速率、价格，也指评价。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reckoned, fixed amount; the senses divide into a measured proportion, a set price, judging, and regarding as.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「经计算而确定的数额」；义项分为测得的比例、定好的价格、评判，以及把……看作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a meter ticking at fixed intervals, its numbers even and regular.
core.cn: 核心意象：按固定间隔跳动的仪表，数字均匀而规律。

latinIntro.en: Latin rata, fixed by reckoning, and the verb reri, to reckon, are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rata（经计算而确定）与动词 reri（计算）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 宁愿；相当；更确切地说
definition_en: more willingly, used in would rather; to a certain degree, fairly; more precisely, used to correct or contrast
core_image: 分岔的小路上脚步偏向更安静的一侧
scene: 路口分出两条小道，脚步不自觉地偏向更安静的那一条。I would rather walk than take the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 rather 用于 would rather，是「宁愿」（第 1 个义项：更愿意做某事）；句意为比起坐公交，我更愿意走路。画面里可留意：分岔的小路、偏向一侧的脚步。

derivatives.zh: rather 加 -ish，指有点儿、稍微
同源的古词，指早的、迅速的

senses.title: More willingly
senses.definition: more willingly, used with would to express a preference
senses.definitionCN: 更愿意，与 would 连用表达偏好
senses.example: I would rather walk than take the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 比起坐公交，我更愿意走路。
senses.why: Old English hraþor meant sooner, and what one chooses sooner is what one prefers, so the word became a marker of preference.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hraþor 意为更早，而人更早选择的正是更偏爱的，于是这个词成了偏好的标记。

senses.title: To a certain degree
senses.definition: to a moderate degree, more than a little but less than very
senses.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，多于一点而少于「很」
senses.example: The film was rather good.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片相当不错。
senses.why: From the sense of more, the word weakened into a plain marker of degree, meaning fairly or quite.
senses.whyCN: 从「更多」的意思出发，这个词弱化为单纯的程度标记，意为「相当」或「颇」。

senses.title: More precisely
senses.definition: used to correct or sharpen what has just been said, or to introduce a better word
senses.definitionCN: 用于更正或精确化刚说过的话，或引出更恰当的说法
senses.example: He is not a teacher, but rather a writer.
senses.exampleCN: 他不是教师，而是作家。
senses.why: When one word is replaced by a better one, the speaker is choosing the preferable term, and rather marks that correction.
senses.whyCN: 当一个词被更恰当的词替换时，说话人正是在选更可取的说法，rather 标记这一更正。

intro.en: Rather is a native English word, the old comparative of an adjective meaning quick or prompt; the idea of sooner grew into the idea of preference.
intro.cn: rather 是英语本族词，原是意为「迅速、敏捷」的形容词的比较级；「更早」的观念长成了「更愿意」。

items.en: Hrathor was the comparative of hræþ, quick or prompt, and meant sooner or more readily.
items.cn: hraþor 是 hræþ（迅速、敏捷）的比较级，意为更早或更乐意。

items.en: Because what one does sooner is what one prefers, the word took on the sense of more willingly.
items.cn: 因为人更早去做的，正是更愿意做的，这个词便带上「更乐意」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rather kept both the older sense of sooner and the newer sense of preference.
items.cn: 中古英语 rather 既保留较早的「更早」，也保留较新的「更愿意」。

items.en: From the idea of more, rather weakened into a word for a moderate degree, meaning fairly.
items.cn: 从「更多」的观念出发，rather 弱化为表示中等程度的词，即「相当」。

items.en: Modern English uses rather in would rather for choice, for moderate degree, and to correct or sharpen a statement.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rather 于 would rather 表选择，表中等程度，以及用来更正或精确化说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers two words often confused with rather and two fixed phrases; the near-meaning group gathers degree words and a word of preference.
note.cn: 形近组收两个易与 rather 混淆的词与两个固定短语；近义组收程度词与一个表偏好的词。

entries.definition: A small rodent, a different word.
A measure or a speed, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 一种比率或速度，另一词。

entries.definition: Instead of, used to set one choice against another.
entries.definitionCN: 而不是，用来把一种选择与另一种对照。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as sooner, becomes more willingly, then a moderate degree, then a correction of words.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「更早」开始，变成「更愿意」，再变成中等程度，最后成为对说法的更正。

normal.en: Rather and rat look alike, but a rat is an animal and rather is a choice or a degree.
normal.cn: rather 与 rat 形近，但 rat 是动物，rather 是选择或程度。

normal.en: Would rather is the phrase for saying what you would prefer.
normal.cn: would rather 是用来说自己更愿意做什么的短语。

normal.en: Rather than sets one choice against another, as in walk rather than drive.
normal.cn: rather than 把一种选择与另一种对照，如 walk rather than drive。

normal.en: Rather good means good to a fair degree, not very good.
normal.cn: rather good 指相当好，而不是非常好。

normal.en: Or rather introduces a better word for what was just said.
normal.cn: or rather 引出对刚说过的话更恰当的说法。

abstract.en: Preference is measured by what you would choose sooner.
abstract.cn: 偏好可以用「你更早选择什么」来衡量。

abstract.en: Rather softens a judgment, leaving room for doubt or modesty.
abstract.cn: rather 让判断变柔，为疑虑或谦逊留出余地。

abstract.en: To correct with rather is to admit that the first word was not quite right.
abstract.cn: 用 rather 更正，就是承认第一个词还不够准确。

examples.en: I would rather stay at home tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚我宁愿待在家里。

examples.en: The film was rather good.
examples.cn: 这部影片相当不错。

examples.en: He is not a teacher, but rather a writer.
examples.cn: 他不是教师，而是作家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「岔路口偏一步」——两条路摆着，脚步偏向更愿意走的那条，记住 rather 是宁愿、相当。

root: 古英语 hræþ（迅速）→ 比较级 hraþor（更早、更乐意）→ 中古英语 rather → 现代英语 rather；同族有 rathe。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a comparison of readiness; the senses move from preference to moderate degree to a correction of wording.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「乐意程度的比较」；义项从宁愿，到中等程度，再到对措辞的更正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fork in a path where the foot leans toward the quieter way.
core.cn: 核心意象：路边出现岔口，脚步偏向更安静的那条路。

branches.en: a foot turning toward one path
branches.cn: 脚步转向其中一条小路

branches.en: a mark halfway up a scale
branches.cn: 刻度尺上居中偏上的标记

branches.en: a word crossed out and replaced
branches.cn: 一个被划掉并替换的词

branches.en: leaning toward a choice and leaning toward a degree
branches.cn: 偏向一种选择，也偏向一个程度

branches.en: softening a claim and correcting a word

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its small family is built from an old comparative ending and fixed phrases.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其不大的词族由古老的比较级词尾与固定短语构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded; the word is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录；这个词是日耳曼语本族词。

definition_zh: 比率；比值；比例关系
definition_en: the relation between two amounts, showing how many times one contains the other; a proportion between parts
core_image: 天平两端各堆砝码，数目清晰可数的对比
scene: 天平两端各放着一堆砝码，数目一眼就能数清。The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
sceneCN: 这里 ratio 是「比率」（第 1 个义项：两个数量之间的倍数关系）；句意为学生与教师的比例是十比一。画面里可留意：天平两端的砝码、清楚的数目对比。

collocations.phrase: the ratio of A to B
collocations.zh: A 与 B 的比率

derivatives.zh: 与 ratio 同源的拉丁词，指定量、配给
ratio 加 -al，指理性的、合理的
rational 加 -e，指理由说明
ratio 加 -cin- 与 -ation，指（正式的）推理

senses.title: The relation between two amounts
senses.definition: the relation between two amounts, showing how many times one contains the other
senses.definitionCN: 两个数量之间的关系，表明一个包含另一个多少次
senses.example: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
senses.exampleCN: 学生与教师的比例是十比一。
senses.why: Latin ratio meant a reckoning, and a reckoning of two amounts against each other is exactly a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ratio 意为计算，而把两个数量相互算一算，正是一个比率。

senses.title: A proportion between parts
senses.definition: a proportion in which parts are compared with one another or with the whole
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相互比较或与整体比较时的比例关系
senses.example: The recipe gives the ratio of flour to water.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱给出了面粉与水的比例。
senses.why: Once two amounts could be compared, the word served for any ordered comparison of parts, as in a recipe or a design.
senses.whyCN: 一旦两个数量可以相互比较，这个词便用于任何有次序的部分比较，如食谱或设计中的配比。

intro.en: Ratio is the Latin word for reckoning, calculation and reason; it comes from reri, to reckon or think, and English borrowed it directly.
intro.cn: ratio 是拉丁语中表示计算、推算与理性的词；它源自动词 reri（计算、思考），英语直接借用了它。

items.en: Ratio meant a reckoning or a calculation, and also the faculty of reason that makes counting possible.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算或推算，也指使计数成为可能的理性能力。

items.en: The verb reri meant to reckon or think, and ratio was the noun of that act.
items.cn: 动词 reri 意为计算或思考，ratio 是这一动作的名词。

items.en: Roman writers used ratio for the relation between numbers, the sense that mathematics still keeps.
items.cn: 罗马作者用 ratio 指数字之间的关系，这一意思仍留在数学中。

items.en: English took ratio straight from Latin in the mathematical and general sense of a relation between amounts.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 ratio，用于数学及一般意义上「数量之间的关系」。

items.en: Modern English uses ratio for a quotient, for a proportion between parts, and in fixed phrases such as the golden ratio.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ratio 指比值、部分之间的比例，并见于 golden ratio 等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin root and one near form; the near-meaning group gathers words for proportion and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根的词与一个近形词；近义组收表示比例与比较的词。

entries.definition: A measure or a speed, related in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一种度量或速度，意义相关。

entries.definition: A fixed share of food or supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 食物或物资的定量份额。

entries.definition: A set of reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事给出的一套理由。

entries.definition: The relation of one part to another or to the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 一部分与另一部分或与整体的关系。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, often written as one number over another.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的一部分，常写成一个数在另一个数之上。

entries.definition: A rate or proportion expressed out of a hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 以百为基数表达的比率或比例。

entries.definition: A part given to or held by one person or group.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人或某群体的一份。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin reckoning, and every sense is a way of putting two amounts side by side to see how they compare.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「计算」，每个义项都是把两个数量并排摆好、看它们如何相比的方式。

normal.en: Ratio and rate both come from reckoning, but ratio compares two amounts while rate measures one against time.
normal.cn: ratio 与 rate 都源于计算，但 ratio 比较两个数量，rate 则用一个量去量时间。

normal.en: The ratio of A to B is written as a pair of numbers, often with a colon.
normal.cn: A 与 B 的比率写成一对数，常用冒号隔开。

normal.en: A recipe works by ratio: so much flour for so much water.
normal.cn: 食谱靠 ratio 运作：多少面粉配多少水。

normal.en: The golden ratio is a fixed proportion that appears in art and nature.
normal.cn: 黄金比例是一个固定的比例，出现在艺术与自然之中。

normal.en: Ration is the same root, a fixed share measured out.
normal.cn: ration 同根，指称量出来的一份定量。

abstract.en: A ratio turns a comparison into a number you can carry away.
abstract.cn: ratio 把一次比较变成一个可以带走的数字。

abstract.en: To give a ratio is to say how much of one thing sits beside another.
abstract.cn: 给出一个 ratio，就是说明一物相对另一物有多少。

abstract.en: Every ratio chooses what to count and what to leave out.
abstract.cn: 每一个 ratio 都在选择数什么、略去什么。

examples.en: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
examples.cn: 学生与教师的比例是十比一。

examples.en: The recipe gives the ratio of flour to water.
examples.cn: 这份食谱给出了面粉与水的比例。

examples.en: Mix the paint in a ratio of two parts blue to one part white.
examples.cn: 按两份蓝配一份白的比例调颜料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞笑」——天平两端一称，数目比出来了，记住 ratio 是比率、比例。

root: 拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）→ 英语 ratio；源自动词 reri（计算、思考）。同根有 rate、ration、rational、rationale。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reckoning of two amounts; the senses divide into a quotient and a proportion between parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是对两个数量的计算；义项分为比值与部分之间的比例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: weights piled on both pans of a balance, their numbers plainly compared.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端堆着砝码，数目清楚地相互比较。

chain: TWO AMOUNTS SET SIDE BY SIDE

branches.en: two piles of weights on a balance
flour and water measured for a recipe
branches.cn: 按食谱量好的面粉与水

branches.en: one quotient and one recipe proportion
branches.cn: 一个比值与一份食谱配比

branches.en: two ways of putting amounts side by side
branches.cn: 把数量并排摆好的两种方式

branches.en: the same reckoning at different scales
branches.cn: 同一套计算在不同尺度上

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with Latin and English suffixes on the root reri.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由 reri 词根上的拉丁语与英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ratio, a reckoning, and reri, to reckon, are the recorded sources of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ratio（计算）与 reri（计算）是这个词族有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 生的；未加工的；生疏的；裸露刺痛的
definition_en: not cooked; not processed or refined; inexperienced and untrained; bare and sore, of skin or nerves
core_image: 刚出矿的粗糙石块，棱角上还粘着砂粒
scene: 采石场里，刚开采出的石块粗糙发灰，棱角上还粘着砂粒。The raw material is shipped to the factory for processing.
sceneCN: 这里 raw 是「未加工的」（第 2 个义项：尚未经过处理或提炼）；句意为原材料被运往工厂加工。画面里可留意：粗糙的石块、棱角的砂粒、运石的车。

pos.zh: 生的；未加工的；生疏的；裸露刺痛的

derivatives.zh: raw 加 -ness，指生、未加工的状态
raw 加 -ly，指生硬地、赤裸地
raw 与 hide 复合，指生皮

senses.title: Not cooked
senses.definition: of food, not cooked at all
senses.definitionCN: 指食物完全没有烹煮
senses.example: Cats can eat raw meat.
senses.exampleCN: 猫可以吃生肉。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply uncooked, and it still describes food taken straight from the fireless kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「未煮」，至今仍用来描述未经火候的食物。

senses.title: Not processed
senses.definition: of a material, not yet treated, refined or manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 指材料尚未经过处理、提炼或制造
senses.example: The raw material is shipped to the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 原材料被运往工厂。
senses.why: From uncooked food the word extended to any material that has not yet been worked into its final form.
senses.whyCN: 从「未煮的食物」扩展到任何尚未被加工成最终形态的材料。

senses.title: Inexperienced
senses.definition: new to something and not yet trained or hardened
senses.definitionCN: 刚接触某事、尚未训练或磨练的
senses.example: The raw recruits were still learning to march.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们还在学习列队行进。
senses.why: A person who has not been through training is like material not yet worked, so raw came to mean inexperienced.
senses.whyCN: 未经训练的人就像尚未加工的材料，于是 raw 引申为「生疏」。

senses.title: Bare and sore
senses.definition: of skin or a nerve, exposed and painful, without protection
senses.definitionCN: 指皮肤或神经外露、疼痛、缺乏保护
senses.example: The cold wind stung his raw face.
senses.exampleCN: 寒风刺着他裸露发疼的脸。
senses.why: Skin stripped of its covering is exposed like unworked material, and the painful openness gave the word its sense of soreness.
senses.whyCN: 失去覆盖的皮肤就像未经处理的材料一样暴露在外，这种疼痛的暴露给了这个词「刺痛」的意思。

intro.en: Raw is a native English word from Old English hreaw, meaning uncooked, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: raw 是英语本族词，来自古英语 hreaw（未煮的），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Hreaw meant uncooked or unprocessed, and it described food and materials alike.
items.cn: hreaw 意为未煮或未加工的，既形容食物，也形容材料。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic languages carry the same sense of something not yet cooked or worked.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语言中的相关形式带有同样的「尚未煮或加工」之意。

items.en: Middle English raw kept the sense of uncooked and extended it to what was rough and unfinished.
items.cn: 中古英语 raw 保留「未煮」的意思，并扩展到粗糙、未完成之物。

items.en: Because what is unworked is also untrained or uncovered, raw came to describe new soldiers and bare skin.
items.cn: 由于未加工之物也意味着未受训练或未被覆盖，raw 便用来形容新兵与裸露的皮肤。

items.en: Modern English uses raw for uncooked food, unprocessed material, inexperienced people, and exposed flesh.
items.cn: 现代英语用 raw 指生食、未加工的材料、无经验的人，以及裸露的皮肉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and one easily confused word; the near-meaning group gathers words for the uncooked, the unrefined and the untrained.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与一个易混词；近义组收表示生的、未精炼的、未受训练的词。

entries.definitionCN: 用生皮制成的未处理皮革。

entries.definition: Lightly cooked, easily confused with raw.
entries.definitionCN: 半熟的，容易与 raw 混淆。

entries.definition: In a natural state, not refined.
entries.definitionCN: 处于自然状态、未经精炼的。

entries.definition: Not treated by an industrial process.
New to an activity, without practice.
entries.definitionCN: 刚接触某项活动、缺乏实践的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as uncooked, then covers unworked material, untrained people and unprotected skin, all sharing the idea of not yet finished.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「未煮」开始，随后覆盖未加工的材料、未受训练的人与未受保护的皮肤，都共享「尚未完成」这一想法。

normal.en: Raw and rare are close in the kitchen, but raw is completely uncooked while rare is lightly cooked.
normal.cn: 在厨房里 raw 与 rare 相近，但 raw 是完全没煮，rare 是略煮。

normal.en: Raw material is what a factory turns into a finished product.
normal.cn: raw material 是工厂加工成成品之前的材料。

normal.en: Raw data has not yet been cleaned or sorted.
normal.cn: raw data 是尚未清理或整理的数据。

normal.en: A raw recruit is a soldier who has not yet been trained.
normal.cn: raw recruit 是尚未受过训练的新兵。

normal.en: Raw skin is skin stripped of its covering and left sore.
normal.cn: raw skin 是失去覆盖、裸露发疼的皮肤。

abstract.en: What is raw is full of possibility but not yet usable.
abstract.cn: raw 之物充满可能，却尚不可用。

abstract.en: To be raw is to be honest and exposed at the same time.
abstract.cn: raw 既是坦诚，也是暴露。

abstract.en: Every finished thing once lay raw and unshaped.
abstract.cn: 每一件成品都曾经是未成形的原材料。

examples.en: Cats can eat raw meat.
examples.cn: 猫可以吃生肉。

examples.en: The raw material is shipped to the factory for processing.
examples.cn: 原材料被运往工厂加工。

examples.en: The raw recruits were still learning to march.
examples.cn: 新兵们还在学习列队行进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「刚从矿里挖出的石块」——粗糙、没加工过，记住 raw 是生的、未加工的。

root: 古英语 hreaw（未煮的）→ 中古英语 raw → 现代英语 raw；同族有 rawness、rawhide、rawboned。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not yet finished; the senses divide into uncooked food, unprocessed material, untrained people, and unprotected skin.

core.cn: 核心意象：刚从采石场切下的粗糙石块，棱角上还粘着砂粒。

branches.en: meat straight from the fireless kitchen
ore and stone at the quarry face

skin stripped bare by the wind
unworked material and untrained people

definition_zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系；可及范围
definition_en: to arrive at a place; to stretch out a hand to touch something; to attain a level or amount; to get in touch with someone; the distance within which something can be reached
core_image: 手臂伸向高架上的一只杯子
scene: 高架上的杯子有点远，手臂伸到极限才碰到杯沿。She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
sceneCN: 这里 reach 是「伸手够到」（第 2 个义项：把手伸出去触到某物）；句意为她用指尖够到了顶层架子。画面里可留意：伸出的手臂、高架上的杯子、碰到的指尖。

pos.zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系

derivatives.zh: reach 加 -able，指可到达的、可联系的
out 与 reach 复合，指主动外联、延伸服务
over- 与 reach 复合，指做得过头、超越能力

senses.title: To arrive at a place
senses.definition: to arrive at a place, especially after effort or a journey
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地，尤指经过努力或一段行程之后
senses.example: We reached the village before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在天黑前到达了村子。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to stretch out to a point, and arriving is stretching your journey until it touches the destination.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「伸到一点」，而抵达就是让行程一直伸到触着目的地。

senses.title: To stretch out and touch
senses.definition: to put out a hand or arm in order to touch or take something
senses.definitionCN: 伸出手或手臂去触到或拿取某物
senses.example: She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
senses.exampleCN: 她用指尖够到了顶层架子。
senses.why: The word first pictured a hand extended until it met an object, and this literal picture is still the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘的是手一直伸到与物体相接，这一字面画面至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To attain a level
senses.definition: to arrive at a particular level, amount or standard after a process
senses.definitionCN: 经过一个过程达到某一水平、数量或标准
senses.example: Sales reached a record high last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月的销售额达到了历史新高。
senses.why: If a hand can reach a height, then a process can reach a level, so the word extended from space to measure.
senses.whyCN: 手能伸到一个高度，一个过程也能达到一个水平，于是这个词从空间扩展到度量。

senses.title: To get in touch
senses.definition: to succeed in speaking or writing to someone
senses.definitionCN: 成功地与某人通话或通信
senses.example: I tried to reach him by phone all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我一上午都在试着打电话联系他。
senses.why: Making contact is like stretching across a distance until the other person is touched, so reach came to mean communicate with.
senses.whyCN: 建立联系就像跨越距离一直伸到触着对方，于是 reach 引申为「与……沟通」。

senses.title: The distance one can reach
senses.definition: the distance or range within which something can be reached or used
senses.definitionCN: 某物能被触及或使用所及的距离或范围
senses.example: The cookies are within the child's reach.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干在孩子够得着的范围内。
senses.why: From the act of stretching came the noun for how far that stretch goes, hence the range one can cover.
senses.whyCN: 从「伸展」的动作生出名词，表示这一伸能到多远，因此就是可覆盖的范围。

intro.en: Reach is a native English word from Old English ræcan, to stretch out or extend, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: reach 是英语本族词，来自古英语 ræcan（伸出、延伸），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Ræcan meant to stretch out or extend toward something, often a hand toward an object.
items.cn: ræcan 意为向某物伸出或延伸，常指手伸向物体。

items.en: Related Germanic verbs carry the same picture of extending toward a point.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语动词带有同样的「朝一点延伸」的画面。

items.en: Middle English reach widened from the hand to the journey, so one could reach a town as well as a shelf.
items.cn: 中古英语 reach 从手扩展到行程，因此既能 reach 一个架子，也能 reach 一座城镇。

items.en: As the word moved from space to levels and to people, it took in reaching a figure and reaching a person.
items.cn: 随着这个词从空间转到水平与人，它纳入了达到某个数字与联系到某个人。

items.en: Modern English uses reach for arriving, stretching, attaining, contacting, and for the range so covered.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reach 表示抵达、伸手、达到、联系，以及由此覆盖的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and fixed phrases; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of arriving, attaining and contacting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与固定短语；近义组收表示抵达、达到与联系的动词。

entries.definition: To extend a hand or make contact.
To stretch a hand toward something.
To go too far or attempt too much.
To reach a level or goal after effort.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力达到某一水平或目标。

entries.definition: To extend a limb or a thing.
To get in touch with someone.

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a hand stretched out, then covers journeys, levels, people and the range so covered.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从伸出的手开始，随后涵盖行程、水平、人，以及由此覆盖的范围。

normal.en: Reach and stretch share the picture of something extended toward a point.
normal.cn: reach 与 stretch 共享「某物朝一点伸展」的画面。

normal.en: You reach a shelf with a hand and reach a city with a journey.
normal.cn: 用手 reach 一个架子，用一段行程 reach 一座城市。

normal.en: Prices reaching a record high is the same word used for a level.
normal.cn: 价格 reaching a record high，是同一个词用在水平上。

normal.en: To reach someone is to stretch across the distance until contact is made.
normal.cn: to reach 某人，就是跨越距离一直伸到建立联系。

normal.en: Within reach means close enough to touch or use.
normal.cn: within reach 意为近得足以触及或使用。

abstract.en: Reach measures the distance between effort and its object.
abstract.cn: reach 衡量的是努力与其目标之间的距离。

abstract.en: What is out of reach is not always out of mind.
abstract.cn: 够不着的东西，并不总是不在心上的。

abstract.en: To reach out is to shorten a distance that other people cannot shorten alone.
abstract.cn: reach out 就是缩短一段别人无法独自缩短的距离。

examples.en: We reached the village before dark.
examples.cn: 我们在天黑前到达了村子。

examples.en: She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
examples.cn: 她用指尖够到了顶层架子。

examples.en: I tried to reach him by phone all morning.
examples.cn: 我一上午都在试着打电话联系他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞奇」——手臂一直伸出去，够到架子上的杯子，记住 reach 是到达、够到。

root: 古英语 ræcan（伸出、延伸）→ 中古英语 reach → 现代英语 reach；同族有 reachable、outreach、overreach。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「朝一点伸展」；义项分为抵达、触到、达到、联系，以及由此覆盖的范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm stretched to its full length toward a cup on a high shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂伸到极限，去够高架上的一只杯子。

branches.en: a traveller arriving at a village gate
fingertips meeting a cup on a shelf
branches.cn: 指尖触到架子上的杯子

branches.en: a graph line climbing to a record
a telephone call that finally connects
a jar placed within a child's grasp
branches.cn: 放在孩子够得着处的罐子

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built with English suffixes, prefixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其词族由英语后缀、前缀与复合词构成。

definition_zh: 反应；作出反应；起化学反应；反对
definition_en: to respond to something that happens; to undergo a chemical change; to act against something in opposition
core_image: 被按到底又猛地弹回的弹簧
scene: 手指一按，弹簧被压到底，松开后立刻弹了回来。The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
sceneCN: 这里 react 是「作出反应」（第 1 个义项：对某事作出回应）；句意为进球时人群报以欢呼。画面里可留意：被压下的弹簧、弹回的瞬间、欢呼的人群。

pos.zh: 反应；作出反应；起化学反应；反对

derivatives.zh: react 加 -ion，指反应、回应
react 加 -or，指反应堆、反应器
react 加 -ive，指易起反应的、反应性的
re- 与 activate 复合，指使重新活跃

senses.title: To respond
senses.definition: to respond in speech, feeling or action to something that has happened
senses.definitionCN: 在言语、情感或行动上对发生之事作出回应
senses.example: The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
senses.exampleCN: 进球时人群报以欢呼。
senses.why: Latin reagere meant to act back, and reacting is exactly acting back upon something that acted first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 reagere 意为「回过来行动」，而 react 正是对先行动的事物回以行动。

senses.title: To undergo chemical change
senses.definition: of substances, to combine or change as a result of a chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 指物质因化学过程而结合或发生变化
senses.example: Sodium reacts violently with water.
senses.exampleCN: 钠与水剧烈反应。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the same idea of acting back: two substances act on each other and are changed by it.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了同一个「相互作用」的想法：两种物质彼此作用并因此改变。

senses.title: To oppose
senses.definition: to act against something one disapproves of or resists
senses.definitionCN: 对自己不赞成或抵抗的事物采取对抗行动
senses.example: Many residents reacted against the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 许多居民反对这项新税。
senses.why: When the action back is directed against a force or a rule, the word takes the sense of resisting or opposing.
senses.whyCN: 当回过来的行动指向某种力量或规则时，这个词便有了「抵抗、反对」的意思。

intro.en: React comes from Latin reagere, built from re-, back, and agere, to do or drive; the word literally means to act back.
intro.cn: react 来自拉丁语 reagere，由 re-（回）与 agere（做、驱动）构成；字面意思就是「回过来行动」。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive or perform, and it is the source of act, action and agent.
items.cn: agere 意为做、驱动或执行，是 act、action、agent 的来源。

items.en: The prefix re- meant back or again, so reagere pictured a force returning upon its source.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 意为向后或再次，因此 reagere 描绘的是一股力量回向它的来源。

items.en: Reagere meant to act back or to respond to an action already under way.
items.cn: reagere 意为回过来行动，或对已经在进行的动作作出回应。

items.en: English took the word as react and applied it to people, to feelings and later to chemical substances.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借作 react，先用于人、情感，后来又用于化学物质。

items.en: Modern English uses react for responses of every kind, for chemical change, and for resistance to what is imposed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 react 指各种回应、化学变化，以及对强加之事的抵抗。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of responding and resisting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式；近义组收表示回应与抵抗的动词。

entries.definition: A response or a chemical change.
A device or plant where a reaction takes place.
entries.definitionCN: 发生反应的装置或设施。

entries.definition: To answer or react to something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事作出回答或反应。

normalIntro.en: The word is literally act back: something acts first, and the response acts upon it in return.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是「回过来行动」：某物先行动，回应再反过来作用于它。

normal.en: React is re- plus act, so it means to act back on what has just happened.
normal.cn: react 是 re- 加 act，意为对刚发生的事回以行动。

normal.en: People react to news, crowds react to a goal, and chemicals react with each other.
normal.cn: 人 react to 消息，人群 react to 进球，化学品彼此 react。

normal.en: React against is the phrase for resisting something you disapprove of.
normal.cn: react against 是表示抵制不赞成之事的短语。

normal.en: Reaction is the noun, reactor the thing where a reaction happens, and reactive the tendency to react.
normal.cn: reaction 是名词，reactor 是发生反应的装置，reactive 是易反应的倾向。

normal.en: A slow reaction and a quick reaction differ in time, not in the word's meaning.
normal.cn: 反应慢与反应快，差别在时间，而不在这个词的意思。

abstract.en: To react is to prove that something outside you has reached you.
abstract.cn: react 就是证明身外之物已经触及了你。

abstract.en: What we react against often tells us what we value.
abstract.cn: 我们反对的东西，常常说明我们看重什么。

abstract.en: Every action leaves the world waiting for a reaction.
abstract.cn: 每一个行动都让世界等着一个回应。

examples.en: The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
examples.cn: 进球时人群报以欢呼。

examples.en: Sodium reacts violently with water.
examples.cn: 钠与水剧烈反应。

examples.en: Many residents reacted against the new tax.
examples.cn: 许多居民反对这项新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞阿克特」——弹簧被按下又弹回，记住 react 是反应、作出反应。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ agere（做、驱动）→ reagere（回过来行动）→ 英语 react；同族有 reaction、reactor、reactive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is acting back; the senses divide into human response, chemical change, and opposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「回过来行动」；义项分为人的回应、化学变化与反对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring pressed down and snapping back as soon as the finger lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：弹簧被压下，手指一松便立刻弹回。

branches.en: a crowd cheering a goal
sodium hissing in water
residents resisting a new tax
a human answer and a chemical answer
branches.cn: 人的回应与化学的回应

branches.en: responding to a change and resisting it
branches.cn: 对变化作出回应，也对其抵抗

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built from re-, agere and English suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由 re-、agere 与英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere, to do, and reagere, to act back, are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere（做）与 reagere（回过来行动）是有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 反应；回应；化学反应；反对
definition_en: a response to something that happens; a chemical change; opposition to a change or idea; an adverse bodily response
core_image: 投入水中的钠块剧烈翻腾
scene: 一小块钠落进水里，立刻嘶嘶作响、四处窜动。Her first reaction was to laugh.
sceneCN: 这里 reaction 是「反应」（第 1 个义项：对刺激的回应）；句意为她的第一反应是大笑。画面里可留意：水中翻腾的钠块、四溅的水花、笑声。

pos.zh: 反应；回应；化学反应；反对

react 加 -or，指反应堆、反应器
react 加 -ive，指易起反应的

senses.title: A response
senses.definition: a response in feeling, speech or action to something that happens
senses.definitionCN: 对发生之事在情感、言语或行动上的回应
senses.example: Her first reaction was to laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一反应是大笑。
senses.why: Reaction is the noun of react, so it names the acting back that follows some earlier event.
senses.whyCN: reaction 是 react 的名词，因此它命名的是在先发生之事之后「回过来的行动」。

senses.title: A chemical change
senses.definition: a process in which substances combine or break down and form new substances
senses.definitionCN: 物质结合或分解、生成新物质的过程
senses.example: The experiment produced a bright chemical reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验产生了明亮的化学反应。
senses.why: Chemistry uses the same noun for substances acting on one another and being changed in return.
senses.whyCN: 化学用同一个名词指物质彼此作用、并因此改变。

senses.title: Opposition to change
senses.definition: a movement or feeling that resists a change, often a political or social one
senses.definitionCN: 抵制某种改变的运动或情绪，常指政治或社会变革
senses.example: The reform met with strong reaction from conservative groups.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革遭到保守团体的强烈反对。
senses.why: When the acting back is turned against a new force, reaction means resistance rather than mere response.
senses.whyCN: 当回过来的行动转而对抗一股新力量时，reaction 便指抵抗，而不只是回应。

senses.title: An adverse bodily response
senses.definition: a harmful or unwanted response of the body to a drug or substance
senses.definitionCN: 身体对药物或物质的有害或不良回应
senses.example: The patient had an allergic reaction to the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 病人对药物产生了过敏反应。
senses.why: A body that reacts badly to a substance produces what medicine calls a reaction, a response that harms rather than helps.
senses.whyCN: 身体对某物质反应不良，就产生医学所称的 reaction，一种有害而无益的回应。

intro.en: Reaction is react plus the Latin noun ending -ion; react itself goes back to Latin reagere, to act back.
intro.cn: reaction 是 react 加拉丁名词词尾 -ion；react 本身可追溯到拉丁语 reagere（回过来行动）。

items.en: Agere meant to do or drive, and action is the noun of that doing.
items.cn: agere 意为做或驱动，action 就是这一动作的名词。

items.en: Reagere meant to act back, and English react kept that picture of a return of force.
items.cn: reagere 意为回过来行动，英语 react 保留了力量回返的画面。

items.en: The Latin ending -ion turned the verb into a noun, giving English reaction as the name of the return act.
items.cn: 拉丁词尾 -ion 把动词变成名词，给英语带来 reaction，作为这一回返动作的名称。

items.en: Chemists adopted the noun for substances that act on one another and are transformed.
items.cn: 化学家采用这个名词，指彼此作用并发生转变的物质。

items.en: Modern English uses reaction for responses of all kinds, chemical change, political resistance and bodily responses to drugs.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reaction 指各种回应、化学变化、政治抵制，以及身体对药物的反应。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on react; the near-meaning group gathers words for responses and resistance.
note.cn: 形近组收由 react 构成的形式；近义组收表示回应与抵抗的词。

entries.definition: To respond or undergo chemical change.
A device where a reaction takes place.
Opposed to change, often in politics.
entries.definitionCN: 反对变革的，常指政治上。

entries.definition: An answer or reply to something.
Information given in return about a result.
entries.definitionCN: 对结果给出的反馈信息。

entries.definition: The act of opposing or withstanding.

normalIntro.en: The noun names whatever comes back after something acts: a feeling, a chemical change, a political pushback or a bodily alarm.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词命名某物行动之后返回的一切：一种情绪、一次化学变化、一次政治反弹，或一次身体警报。

normal.en: Reaction is react with -ion, the noun for the act of acting back.
normal.cn: reaction 是 react 加 -ion，是「回过来行动」这一动作的名词。

normal.en: A first reaction is the response that comes before thinking.
normal.cn: first reaction 是思考之前先来的回应。

normal.en: A chemical reaction is two substances acting on each other.
normal.cn: chemical reaction 是两种物质彼此作用。

normal.en: A chain reaction is one reaction setting off the next.
normal.cn: chain reaction 是一次反应引发下一次。

normal.en: An adverse reaction is a response that harms the body.
normal.cn: adverse reaction 是伤害身体的回应。

abstract.en: Every reaction is evidence that an earlier action landed somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每一个 reaction 都证明先前的行动落在了某处。

abstract.en: Reaction against change often begins as fear of loss.
abstract.cn: 对变革的 reaction 常常始于对失去的恐惧。

abstract.en: A reaction can be measured, but its meaning must be read.
abstract.cn: 反应可以测量，其含义却需要解读。

examples.en: Her first reaction was to laugh.
examples.cn: 她的第一反应是大笑。

examples.en: The experiment produced a bright chemical reaction.
examples.cn: 这个实验产生了明亮的化学反应。

examples.en: The patient had an allergic reaction to the drug.
examples.cn: 病人对药物产生了过敏反应。

a crowd resisting a reform
a rash spreading after a drug
a human answer and a chemical answer

definition_zh: 阅读；朗读；理解；显示
definition_en: to look at and understand written words; to say written words aloud; to interpret or understand a situation; to show a measurement, of an instrument
core_image: 灯光下一页翻开、字行清晰的书
scene: 台灯下，书页被轻轻翻开，一行行字在光里清清楚楚。She read the letter twice before answering.
sceneCN: 这里 read 是「阅读」（第 1 个义项：看文字并理解其意思）；句意为她把信读了两遍才回复。画面里可留意：台灯的光、翻开的书页、清晰的字行。

derivatives.zh: read 加 -er，指读者、读本
read 加 -ing，指阅读、读数
read 加 -able，指可读的、易读的
read 与 out 复合，指读数显示

senses.title: To understand written words
senses.definition: to look at written or printed words and understand their meaning
senses.definitionCN: 看书面或印刷的文字并理解其意思
senses.example: She read the letter twice before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信读了两遍才回复。
senses.why: Old English rædan meant to interpret and advise, and understanding written marks is a form of interpreting them.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 rædan 意为解释与建议，而理解书写的符号正是解释它们的一种方式。

senses.title: To say aloud
senses.definition: to speak written words aloud, especially to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 把书面文字大声说出，尤指读给听众
senses.example: He read the poem to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他给全班朗读了这首诗。
senses.why: Reading aloud adds the voice to the act of understanding, so the same verb covers both silent and spoken reading.
senses.whyCN: 朗读在理解的动作上加了声音，于是同一个动词既指默读，也指出声读。

senses.title: To interpret
senses.definition: to understand or judge a situation, a person or a sign in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式理解或判断形势、人或迹象
senses.example: She read his silence as disapproval.
senses.exampleCN: 她把他的沉默理解为不赞成。
senses.why: Because reading is interpreting marks, the verb naturally extends to interpreting anything that carries a meaning.
senses.whyCN: 既然阅读就是解释符号，这个动词便自然扩展到解释任何携带意义之物。

senses.title: To show a measurement
senses.definition: of an instrument, to show a particular figure or value
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器显示出某个数字或数值
senses.example: The thermometer read thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示三十度。
senses.why: An instrument's dial is like a line of writing that must be read, so the verb came to mean what a gauge shows.
senses.whyCN: 仪器的表盘就像一行需要读取的文字，于是这个动词也指仪表所显示的内容。

intro.en: Read is a native English word from Old English rædan, to advise, interpret or read, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: read 是英语本族词，来自古英语 rædan（劝告、解释、阅读），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Rædan meant to advise, interpret or explain, and reading written marks was one kind of interpretation.
items.cn: rædan 意为劝告、解释或说明，而阅读书写符号是解释的一种。

items.en: Related Germanic words tie the verb to counsel and to the solving of a riddle.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语词把这个动词与劝告、猜解谜语联系起来。

items.en: Middle English read narrowed toward the reading of texts, while the older sense of counsel faded.
items.cn: 中古英语 read 向「读文本」收窄，较早的「劝告」之义逐渐消失。

items.en: The verb grew to cover reading aloud and interpreting signs, since both are ways of giving meaning to marks.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到朗读与解读迹象，因为两者都是赋予符号意义的方式。

items.en: Modern English uses read for texts, for spoken reading, for interpreting situations, and for what gauges show.
items.cn: 现代英语用 read 指文本、出声读、解读形势，以及仪表所显示的内容。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of studying, scanning and interpreting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与复合词；近义组收表示研读、浏览与解读的动词。

entries.definition: The act of reading, or a figure shown.
entries.definitionCN: 阅读的行为，或显示的数值。

entries.definition: To read and learn about a subject.
To explain the meaning of something.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as interpreting marks, then covers silent reading, reading aloud, reading a situation, and reading a gauge.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「解释符号」开始，随后涵盖默读、朗读、解读形势与读取仪表。

normal.en: Read a book and read a situation use the same verb because both mean interpreting signs.
normal.cn: read a book 与 read a situation 用同一个动词，因为两者都是解释符号。

normal.en: Read aloud adds a voice to the act of understanding written words.
normal.cn: read aloud 在理解文字的动作上加了声音。

normal.en: Read between the lines means to find meaning that is not written down.
normal.cn: read between the lines 意为找出没有明写的含义。

normal.en: A gauge reads a figure the way a page reads a sentence.
normal.cn: 仪表 reads 一个数字，就像书页 reads 一句话。

normal.en: Reader and reading come straight from read, one for the person and one for the act.
normal.cn: reader 与 reading 直接来自 read，一个指人，一个指行为。

abstract.en: To read is to let marks become meaning.
abstract.cn: read 就是让符号变成意义。

abstract.en: What we read in a silence says more about us than about the silence.
abstract.cn: 我们从沉默中读到的东西，更多说明我们自己，而不是沉默。

abstract.en: Every reading is a choice of which marks to notice.
abstract.cn: 每一次阅读都是在选择注意哪些符号。

examples.en: She read the letter twice before answering.
examples.cn: 她把信读了两遍才回复。

examples.en: He read the poem to the class.
examples.cn: 他给全班朗读了这首诗。

examples.en: The thermometer read thirty degrees.
examples.cn: 温度计显示三十度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞德」——台灯下翻开的书页，字行清清楚楚，记住 read 是阅读、朗读。

root: 古英语 rædan（劝告、解释、阅读）→ 中古英语 read → 现代英语 read；同族有 reader、reading、readable、readout。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is interpreting marks; the senses divide into reading text, reading aloud, interpreting a situation, and reading a gauge.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「解释符号」；义项分为阅读文本、朗读、解读形势，以及读取仪表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page opened under a lamp, its lines clear in the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下一页翻开的书，字行在光里清清楚楚。

branches.en: a letter read twice before a reply
a poem spoken to a class
silence taken as disapproval
branches.cn: 被理解为不赞成的沉默

branches.en: a thermometer showing thirty degrees
reading words and reading signs

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built with English suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其词族由英语后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 读者；读本；读取器；审稿人
definition_en: a person who reads; a book of texts for learning a language or subject; a device that reads data; a person who reads and comments on manuscripts
core_image: 图书馆窗边低头翻书的人
scene: 图书馆的窗边，一个人低着头，一页页翻着手中的书。The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
sceneCN: 这里 reader 是「读者」（第 1 个义项：阅读书刊的人）；句意为这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。画面里可留意：窗边的座位、低头翻书的人、摊开的书页。

pos.zh: 读者；读本；读取器；审稿人

derivatives.zh: reader 去掉 -er，指阅读
read 加 -ing，指阅读、读数

senses.title: A person who reads
senses.definition: a person who reads books, magazines or other texts
senses.definitionCN: 阅读书籍、杂志或其他文本的人
senses.example: The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。
senses.why: Reader is simply read plus the agent ending -er, so it names the one who performs the act of reading.
senses.whyCN: reader 就是 read 加施动词尾 -er，因此它命名的是执行阅读这一动作的人。

senses.title: A book for learning
senses.definition: a book containing texts chosen for learning a language or a subject
senses.definitionCN: 为学习语言或某科目而编选的文本汇编
senses.example: The class worked through a French reader.
senses.exampleCN: 全班学完了一本法语读本。
senses.why: A book made to be read by learners was called a reader, because the book itself is meant for reading practice.
senses.whyCN: 为学习者编的书被称为 reader，因为这本书本身就是供阅读练习用的。

senses.title: A device that reads data
senses.definition: a machine or device that reads information from cards, discs or codes
senses.definitionCN: 从卡片、光盘或代码中读取信息的机器或装置
senses.example: The guard swiped the card through the reader.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫把卡在读卡器上刷了一下。
senses.why: The agent ending was extended to machines, since a device that reads data performs the same act as a person reading it.
senses.whyCN: 施动词尾被扩展到机器，因为读取数据的装置与读数据的人执行同一个动作。

senses.title: A manuscript reviewer
senses.definition: a person employed to read and comment on manuscripts for a publisher
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为出版社阅读并评议稿件的人
senses.example: The manuscript was sent to an outside reader.
senses.exampleCN: 稿子被送给一位外审。
senses.why: In publishing, the person who reads a manuscript before it is accepted performs the act of reading as a job, hence the title reader.
senses.whyCN: 在出版业，接受前阅读稿子的人以阅读为职业，因此得到 reader 这个称号。

intro.en: Reader is formed in English from the verb read and the agent ending -er, and the verb itself goes back to Old English rædan.
intro.cn: reader 由英语动词 read 与施动词尾 -er 构成，而这个动词可追溯到古英语 rædan。

items.en: Old English had rædere for a reader or interpreter, formed from rædan, to read or explain.
items.cn: 古英语已有 rædere，指读者或解释者，由 rædan（阅读、解释）构成。

items.en: The ending -er marks the one who does an action, so read plus -er is the one who reads.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 标记执行动作的人，因此 read 加 -er 就是阅读的人。

items.en: Middle English reader kept the sense of a person who reads and began to name books meant for reading practice.
items.cn: 中古英语 reader 保留「阅读的人」之意，并开始指供阅读练习的书。

items.en: Modern use extended the word to machines that read data and to people paid to read manuscripts.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词扩展到读取数据的机器，以及受雇阅读稿件的人。

items.en: Modern English uses reader for the person, the learning book, the device and the manuscript reviewer.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reader 指人、学习读本、读取器与审稿人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on read; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who receive texts.
note.cn: 形近组收由 read 构成的形式；近义组收表示接收文本的人。

entries.definition: The collective readers of a publication.
The people reached by a book, film or speech.
entries.definitionCN: 书、电影或演讲所触及的人群。

entries.definition: A person who pays to receive a publication.
entries.definitionCN: 付费订阅某出版物的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is read plus -er, and the ending has stretched from people to books, machines and manuscript reviewers.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 read 加 -er，这个词尾已从人扩展到书、机器与审稿人。

normal.en: Reader is read plus -er, so it names whoever or whatever does the reading.
normal.cn: reader 是 read 加 -er，命名做阅读的人或物。

normal.en: A regular reader comes back to the same magazine issue after issue.
normal.cn: regular reader 一期又一期地回到同一本杂志。

normal.en: A graded reader is a book written at a controlled level for learners.
normal.cn: graded reader 是按受控难度为学习者写的书。

normal.en: A card reader reads the stripe on a card the way a person reads a page.
normal.cn: card reader 读卡片上的磁条，就像人读书页。

normal.en: Readership is the whole body of readers taken together.
normal.cn: readership 是把全体读者合在一起看。

abstract.en: A reader is not a passive receiver but a maker of meaning.
abstract.cn: 读者不是被动的接收者，而是意义的制作者。

abstract.en: Every text has as many readers as it has readings.
abstract.cn: 每个文本有多少种读法，就有多少个读者。

abstract.en: To be a good reader is to notice what the text leaves out.
abstract.cn: 做一个好读者，就是注意到文本省略了什么。

examples.en: The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
examples.cn: 这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。

examples.en: The class worked through a French reader.
examples.cn: 全班学完了一本法语读本。

examples.en: The guard swiped the card through the reader.
examples.cn: 警卫把卡在读卡器上刷了一下。

root: 古英语 rædan（阅读、解释）→ 英语 read + 施动后缀 -er → reader；同族有 read、reading、readable、readership。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one who reads; the senses divide into a person, a learning book, a reading device, and a manuscript reviewer.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「阅读者」；义项分为人、学习读本、读取装置与审稿人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure by a library window, head down, turning one page after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：图书馆窗边的一个人，低头一页页翻书。

a graded reader on a school desk
a card sliding through a reader
a manuscript handed to an outside reader
a person reading and a machine reading

intro.cn: 这个词由本族动词与一个能产的施动词尾在英语中构成。
